glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.heading: Glossary
A
glossary.paragraph: The matrix $\text{adj~}A$ formed from a square matrix $A$ by replacing the $\left( {i,j} \right)\text{-entry}$ of $A$ by the $\left( {i,j} \right)\text{-cofactor}$, for all $i$ and $j$, and then transposing the resulting matrix.
A set that contains all the vectors in any affine combination of any two vectors from the set.
A linear combination of vectors (points in ${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$) in which the sum of the weights involved is $1$.
An equation of the form $c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + \cdots + c_{p}\textbf{v}_{p} = \textbf{0}$, where the weights $c_{1}$,$\ldots$, $c_{p}$ are not all zero, and $c_{1} + \cdots + c_{p} = 0$.

paragraph.strong: affine hull (or affine span) of a set

glossary.paragraph: The set of all affine combinations of points in $S$, denoted by $\text{aff~}S$.

A set $\left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$ in ${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$ such that there are real numbers $c_{1}$,$\ldots$, $c_{p}$, not all zero, such that $c_{1} + \cdots + c_{p} = 0$ and $c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + \cdots + c_{p}\textbf{v}_{p} = \textbf{0}$.
A set $\left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$ in ${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$ that is not affinely dependent.
A set $S$ of points such that if $\textbf{p}$ and $\textbf{q}$ are in $S$, then $(1 - t)\textbf{p} + t\textbf{q} \in S$ for each real number $t$.
A mapping $T:\textbf{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\textbf{ℝ}^{m}$ of the form $T(\textbf{x}) = A\textbf{x} + \textbf{b}$, with $A$ an $m \times n$ matrix and $\textbf{b}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{m}$.
The multiplicity of an eigenvalue as a root of the characteristic equation.
The angle $\vartheta$ between the two directed line segments from the origin through the points $\textbf{u}$ and $\textbf{v}$ is related to the scalar product by
$A(BC) = (AB)C$, for all $A$, $B$, $C$.
The origin when all trajectories tend toward $\textbf{0}$.

A matrix made up of a coefficient matrix for a linear system and one or more columns to the right. Each extra column contains the constants from the right side of a system with the given coefficient matrix.
A type of digital signal processor used to give a more acoustic quality to virtually generated sounds.
A polynomial equation in a variable $r$, created from the coefficients of a homogeneous difference equation.
glossary.heading: B
glossary.paragraph: back-substitution(with matrix notation)
The backward phase of row reduction of an augmented matrix that transforms an echelon matrix into a reduced echelon matrix; used to find the solution(s) of a system of linear equations.
backward phase (of row reduction)
The last part of the algorithm that reduces a matrix in echelon form to a reduced echelon form.
A matrix whose nonzero entries lie within a band along the main diagonal.
The (unique) set of weights needed to write a point as a linear combination of an affinely independent set so the weights sum to $1$.
A variable in a linear system that corresponds to a pivot column in the coefficient matrix.
basis(for a nontrivial subspace $H$ of a vector space $V)$

An indexed set $B = \left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$﻿ in $V$﻿ such that: (i) ﻿$B$ is a linearly independent set and (ii) the subspace spanned by $B$﻿ coincides with ﻿$H$, that is, $H = \text{Span}\left\{ \textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p} \right\}$﻿.
The coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{x}$ ﻿as a linear combination of the vectors in the given basis $B$.﻿
The closest point in a given subspace to a given vector.
The matrix whose columns are the polynomial coefficients of the control points of a Bézier curve.
block diagonal(matrix)
A partitioned matrix $A = \lbrack A_{ij}\rbrack$ such that each block $A_{ij}$ is a zero matrix for $i \neq j$.
A matrix whose entries are themselves matrices of appropriate sizes.
The row–column multiplication of partitioned matrices using the block structure.
block upper triangular(matrix)
A partitioned matrix $A = \lbrack A_{ij}\rbrack$ such that each block $A_{ij}$ is a zero matrix for $i > j$.
For given set $S$, a point $\textbf{p}$ such that every open ball in ${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$ centered at $\textbf{p}$ intersects both $S$ and the complement of $S$.
A set that is contained in an open ball $B(\textbf{0},\delta)$ for some $\delta\operatorname{\& gt;}0$.

A matrix $\lbrack T\rbrack_{B}$ (or $B$-matrix) for a linear transformation $T:V\rightarrow V$ relative to a basis $B$ for $V$, with the property that $\lbrack T(\textbf{x})\rbrack_{B} = \lbrack T\rbrack_{B}\lbrack\textbf{x}\rbrack_{B}$ for all $\textbf{x}$ in V.
The coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{x}$ as a linear combination of the vectors in the given basis $B$.
glossary.heading: C
glossary.paragraph: The matrix generated to test whether a set of signals is linearly independent.
The determinant of the Casorati Matrix.
$\left| \left\langle \textbf{u},\textbf{v} \right\rangle \middle| \leq \left\| u \right\| \cdot \left\| v \right\| \right.$ for all $\textbf{u}$, $\mathbf{v}$.

A matrix $\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$ that transforms $B\text{-coordinate}$ vectors into $C\text{-coordinate}$ vectors: $\left\lbrack \textbf{x} \right\rbrack_{C} = \underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}\left\lbrack \textbf{x} \right\rbrack{}_{B}.$ If $C$ is the standard basis for $\text{ℝ}^{n}$, then $\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$ is sometimes written as $P_{B}$.
change-of-coordinates matrix(from a basis﻿﻿$B$﻿ to a basis﻿﻿$C$﻿)

A matrix $\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$ that transforms $B\text{-coordinate}$ vectors into $C\text{-coordinate}$ vectors: $\left\lbrack \textbf{x} \right\rbrack_{C} = \underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}\left\lbrack \textbf{x} \right\rbrack{}_{B}.$ If $C$ is the standard basis for $\text{ℝ}^{n}$, then $\underset{C\leftarrow B}{P}$ is sometimes written as $P_{B}$.
The equation created by setting the characteristic polynomial to zero.
The polynomial created by subtracting a variable times the identity from a square matrix, and then taking the determinant.
A factorization $A = R^{T}R$﻿﻿ , where $R$ ﻿﻿ is an invertible upper triangular matrix whose diagonal entries are all positive.
A set that contains all of its boundary points.
codomain(of a transformation$T:\text{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\text{ℝ}^{m}$﻿)
The set $\text{ℝ}^{m}$ that contains the range of $T$. In general, if $T$ maps a vector space $V$ into a vector space $W$﻿, then $W$ is called the codomain of $T$.
The numbers (or parameters) multiplied by a variable in a system of equations.
A matrix whose entries are the coefficients of a system of linear equations.
A number $C_{ij} = ( - 1)^{i + j}\det A_{ij}$, called the $(i,j)\text{-cofactor}$ of $A$, where $A_{ij}$ is the submatrix formed by deleting the $i\text{th}$ row and the $j\text{th}$ column of $A$.
A formula for $\det A$ using cofactors associated with one row or one column, such as for row $1$:
The expression of a product $AB$ as a sum of outer products: $\text{col}_{1}(A)\text{row}_{1}(B) + \cdots + \text{col}_{n}(A)\text{row}_{n}(B)$, where $n$ is the number of columns of $A$.

For an $m \times n$ matrix $A$, the set $\text{Col~}A$ of all linear combinations of the columns of $A$. If $A = \left\lbrack {\mathbf{a}_{1}\cdots\mathbf{a}_{n}} \right\rbrack$, then $\text{Col~}A = \text{Span~}\left\{ {\mathbf{a}_{1}\cdots\mathbf{a}_{n}} \right\}$. Equivalently, $$\text{Col~}A = \left\{ {\mathbf{y}:\mathbf{y} = A\mathbf{x}\text{~for~some~}\mathbf{x}\text{~in~}{\mathbb{R}}^{n}} \right\}$$
The sum of the entries in a column of a matrix.
A matrix with only one column, or a single column of a matrix that has several columns.
Two matrices $A$ and $B$ such that ﻿$AB = BA$.
A set in ${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$ that is both closed and bounded.
A special form of matrix whose characteristic polynomial is $( - 1)^{n}p(\lambda)$ when $p(\lambda)$ is a specified polynomial whose leading term is $\lambda^{n}$.
A nonreal root of the characteristic equation of an $n \times n$ matrix.
A nonzero vector $\textbf{x}$ in $\textbf{C}^{n}$ such that $A\textbf{x} = \lambda\textbf{x}$, where $A$ is an $n \times n$ matrix and $\lambda$ is a complex eigenvalue.
The vector orthogonal to $\textbf{u}$ when $\textbf{y}$ is written as the sum of a vector in the direction of $\textbf{u}$ and a vector orthogonal to $\textbf{u}$.

A mapping produced by applying two or more linear transformations in succession. If the transformations are matrix transformations, say left-multiplication by $B$ followed by left-multiplication by $A$﻿, then the composition is the mapping $\textbf{x}\mapsto A(B\textbf{x})$.

The quotient $\sigma_{1}/\sigma_{n}$, where $\sigma_{1}$ is the largest singular value of $A$ and $\sigma_{n}$ is the smallest singular value. The condition number is $+ \infty$ when $\sigma_{n}$ is zero.
Two partitioned matrices $A$ and $B$ such that the block product $AB$ is defined: The column partition of $A$ must match the row partition of $B$.
Refers to a system of equations that has at least one solution.
A linear system with at least one solution.

The problem of maximizing a quantity such as $\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$ or $\parallel A\textbf{x} \parallel$ when $\textbf{x}$ is subject to one or more constraints, such as $\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1$ or $\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{v} = 0$.
A matrix in the Leontief input–output model whose columns are the unit consumption vectors for the various sectors of an economy.
A mapping $\textbf{x}\mapsto r\textbf{x}$ for some scalar $r$, with $0 \leq r \leq 1$.
The matrix used to tell if a pair of matrices is controllable.
controllable(pair of matrices)
Related to a state-space model of a control system and the difference equation ﻿$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k} + B\textbf{u}_{k}\textbf{~}(k = 0,1,\ldots)$.
convergent(sequence of vectors)
A sequence $\mathbf{\left\{ \text{x}_{k} \right\}}$ such that the entries in $\textbf{x}_{k}$ can be made as close as desired to the entries in some fixed vector for all $k$ sufficiently large.
A linear combination of vectors (points) in which the weights in the combination are nonnegative and the sum of the weights is ﻿$1$.
The set of all convex combinations of points in given set $S$﻿, denoted by: $\text{conv~}S$﻿.
A set $S$ with the property that for each $\textbf{p}$ and $\textbf{q}$ in $S$﻿, the line segment $\textbf{pq}$ is contained in ﻿$S$.
coordinate mapping (determined by an ordered basis $B$ in a vector space $V$)
A mapping that associates to each $\textbf{x}$﻿﻿ in ﻿﻿$V$ its coordinate vector $\lbrack\textbf{x}\rbrack_{B}$.﻿
The coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{x}$ as a linear combination of the vectors in the given basis $B$.
The coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{x}$ as a linear combination of the vectors in the given basis $B$.
The vector $\lbrack\textbf{x}\rbrack_{B}$ whose entries are the coordinates of $\textbf{x}$ relative to the basis $B$.
The entry $s_{ij}$ in the covariance matrix $S$ for a matrix of observations, where $x_{i}$ and $x_{j}$ vary over the $i{th}$ and $j{th}$ coordinates, respectively, of the observation vectors.
The $p \times p$ matrix $S$ defined by $S = (N - 1)^{- 1}BB^{T}$, where $B$ is a $p \times N$ matrix of observations in mean-deviation form.
A formula for each entry in the solution $\textbf{x}$ of the equation $A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$ when $A$ is an invertible matrix.
A term $cx_{i}x_{j}$ in a quadratic form, with $i \neq j$﻿.
glossary.heading: D
glossary.paragraph: A difference equation $\textbf{y}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{y}_{k}$, or a differential equation $\textbf{y}^{\prime}(t) = A\textbf{y}(t)$, in which $A$ is a diagonal matrix. The discrete evolution of each entry in $\textbf{y}_{k}$ (as a function of $k$), or the continuous evolution of each entry in the vector-valued function $\textbf{y}(t)$, is unaffected by what happens to the other entries as $k\rightarrow\infty$ or $t\rightarrow\infty$.
The matrix $X$ in the linear model $\mathbf{y = x}\mathbf{\beta}\mathbf{+}\mathbf{\in}$, where the columns of $X$ are determined in some way by the observed values of some independent variables.
A number calculated for a square matrix by following a specified formula.
diagonal entries(in a matrix)
Entries having equal row and column indices.
diagonalizable(matrix)
A matrix that can be written in factored form as $PDP^{- 1}$, where $D$ is a diagonal matrix and $P$ is an invertible matrix.
A square matrix whose entries not on the main diagonal are all zero.
difference equation(orlinear recurrence relation)
An equation of the form $\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$ ($k = 0$, $1$, $2$, $\ldots$) whose solution is a sequence of vectors, $\textbf{x}_{0}$, $\textbf{x}_{1}$, $\ldots$.
A mapping $\textbf{x}\mapsto r\textbf{x}$ for some scalar $r$, with $1 < r$.

list.item: of a flat S﻿: The dimension of the corresponding parallel subspace.
of a set ﻿S: The dimension of the smallest flat containing ﻿S.
of a subspace S﻿: The number of vectors in a basis for ﻿S, written as ﻿dimS.
of a vector space V: The number of vectors in a basis for V﻿, written as ﻿dimV. The dimension of the zero space is ﻿0.﻿

glossary.paragraph: A difference equation of the form $\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$ that describes the changes in a system (usually a physical system) as time passes. The physical system is measured at discrete times, when $k = 0$, $1$, $2$, $\ldots$, and the state of the system at time $k$ is a vector $\textbf{x}_{k}$ whose entries provide certain facts of interest about the system.
The length of the vector $\textbf{u} - \textbf{v}$, denoted by $\text{dist~\,}(\textbf{u},\textbf{v})$.
(left) $A(B + C) = AB + AC$, and (right) $(B + C)A = BA + CA$, for all $A$, $B$, $C$.
domain (of a transformation$T$)
The set of all vectors $\textbf{x}$ for which $T(\textbf{x})$ is defined.

The scalar $\textbf{u}^{T}\textbf{v}$, usually written as $\textbf{u} \cdot \textbf{v}$, where $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are vectors in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ viewed as $n \times 1$ matrices. Also called the dot product of $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$. In general, a function on a vector space that assigns to each pair of vectors $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ a number $\langle\textbf{u},\textbf{v}\rangle$, subject to certain axioms.

A difference equation of the form $\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$ that describes the changes in a system (usually a physical system) as time passes. The physical system is measured at discrete times, when $k = 0$, $1$, $2$, $\ldots$, and the state of the system at time $k$ is a vector $\textbf{x}_{k}$ whose entries provide certain facts of interest about the system.
glossary.heading: E
glossary.paragraph: echelon form(or row echelon form, of a matrix)
An echelon matrix that is row equivalent to the given matrix.
echelon matrix(or row echelon matrix)

A rectangular matrix that has three properties: (1) All nonzero rows are above any row of all zeros. (2) Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it. (3) All entries in a column below a leading entry are zero.

For a differential equation $\textbf{x}^{\prime}(t) = A\textbf{x}(t)$, a function $\textbf{x}(t) = \textbf{v}e^{\lambda t}$, where v is an eigenvector of $A$ and $\lambda$ is the corresponding eigenvalue.
The zero vector together with all the eigenvectors associated with a particular eigenvalue.
For a square matrix $A$, a scalar $\lambda$ such that the equation $A\textbf{x} = \lambda\textbf{x}$ has a nonzero solution.
For a square matrix $A$, a nonzero vector $\textbf{x}$ such that there is a scalar $\lambda$ so that $A\textbf{x} = \lambda\textbf{x}$.
A basis consisting entirely of eigenvectors of a given matrix.
An equation, $\textbf{x} = c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + \cdots + c_{n}\textbf{v}_{n}$, expressing $\textbf{x}$ as a linear combination of eigenvectors of a matrix.
An invertible matrix that results by performing one elementary row operation on an identity matrix.
(1) (Replacement) Replace one row by the sum of itself and a multiple of another row. (2) Interchange two rows. (3) (Scaling) Multiply all entries in a row by a nonzero constant.
Two vectors or matrices that are the same size and their corresponding entries are equal.
A set of prices for the total output of the various sectors in an economy, such that the income of each sector exactly balances its expenses.
A probability vector $\textbf{q}$ such that﻿ $P\textbf{q} = \textbf{q}$.﻿
Linear systems with the same solution set.
See Leontief exchange model.
Asks, “Does a solution to the system exist?” That is, “Is the system consistent?” Also, “Does a solution of $A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$ exist for all possible $\textbf{b}$?”
A formula for $\det A$ using cofactors associated with one row or one column, such as for row $1$:
The sum of the payoffs for a particular pair of strategies.

A point $\textbf{p}$ in $S$ such that $\textbf{p}$ is not in the interior of any line segment that lies in $S$. (That is, if $\textbf{x}$, $\textbf{y}$ are in $S$ and $\textbf{p}$ is on the line segment $\overset{‾}{\textbf{x}\textbf{y}}$, then $\textbf{p} = \textbf{x}$ or $\textbf{p} = \textbf{y}$.)
glossary.heading: F
glossary.paragraph: A vector that satisfies all the linear inequalities.
The set feasible solutions.
final demand vector (orbill of final demands)

The vector $\textbf{d}$ in the Leontief input–output model that lists the dollar values of the goods and services demanded from the various sectors by the nonproductive part of the economy. The vector $\textbf{d}$ can represent consumer demand, government consumption, surplus production, exports, or other external demand.
finite-dimensional (vector space)
A vector space that is spanned by a finite set of vectors.
The set of signals where only finitely many entries of each signal are nonzero.
A translate of a subspace of ${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$.
A matrix whose $j\text{th}$ column gives the deflections of an elastic beam at specified points when a unit force is applied at the $j\text{th}$ point on the beam.

Arithmetic with numbers represented as decimals $\pm .d_{1}\cdots d_{p} \times 10^{r}$, where $r$ is an integer and the number $p$ of digits to the right of the decimal point is usually between $8$ and $16$.
One arithmetic operation $( + , - , \ast ,/)$ on two real floating point numbers.
forward phase (of row reduction)
The first part of the row reduction algorithm that reduces a matrix to echelon form.
An approximation to a function using a trigonometric polynomial.
The weights used to make a trigonometric polynomial as a Fourier approximation to a function.
An infinite series that converges to a function in the inner product space $C\lbrack 0,2\pi\rbrack$, with the inner product given by a definite integral.
Any variable in a linear system that is not a basic variable.
An $m \times n$ matrix whose rank is the smaller of $m$ and $n$.
A basis for the set of all solutions of a homogeneous linear difference or differential equation.
The null space and column space of $A$, and the null space and column space of $A^{T}$, with $\text{Col\,\,\,}A^{T}$ commonly called the row space of $A$.
glossary.heading: G
glossary.paragraph: A systematic method using elementary row operations that reduces a matrix to echelon form or reduced echelon form.
The matrix whose columns are the control points of a Bézier curve.

Given an $m \times n$ matrix $A$ and a vector $\textbf{b}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{m}$, find $\widehat{\textbf{x}}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ such that $\parallel \textbf{b} - A\widehat{\textbf{x}} \parallel \,\, \leq \,\, \parallel \textbf{b} - A\textbf{x} \parallel$ for all $\textbf{x}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$.
general solution(of a linear system)
A parametric description of a solution set that expresses the basic variables in terms of the free variables (the parameters), if any.
A linear transformation from $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ to $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ used in computer programs to create zero entries in a vector (usually a column of a matrix).
A set $\left\lbrack {f:d} \right\rbrack = \left\{ {\textbf{x} \in \textbf{ℝ}^{n}:f\left( \textbf{x} \right) = d} \right\}$
Gram matrix(of $A$)
The matrix $A^{T}A$.
An algorithm for producing an orthogonal or orthonormal basis for a subspace that is spanned by a given set of vectors.
glossary.heading: H
glossary.paragraph: The matrix created when the Hermite polynomials are used as the basis to describe a curve.
Refers to the case where a system of equations, written in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$, has $\mathbf{b} = 0$.

In $\textbf{ℝ}^{3}$, the representation of $(x,y,z)$ as $(X,Y,Z,H)$ for any $H \neq 0$, where $x = X/H$, $y = Y/H$, and $z = Z/H$. In $\textbf{ℝ}^{2}$, $H$ is usually taken as $1$, and the homogeneous coordinates of $(x,y)$ are written as $(x,y,1)$.
homogeneous form $\textbf{v}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$:﻿
The point $\overset{\sim}{v} = \begin{bmatrix} \textbf{v} \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n + 1}$.
A transformation $\textbf{x}\mapsto Q\textbf{x}$, where $Q = I - 2\textbf{uu}^{T}$ and $\textbf{u}$ is a unit vector $(\textbf{u}^{T}\textbf{u} = 1)$.
A flat in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ of dimension $n - 1$. Also: a translate of a subspace of dimension $n - 1$.
glossary.heading: I
glossary.paragraph: identity matrix(denoted by $I$ or $I_{n}$)
A square matrix with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
A square matrix with a large (or possibly infinite) condition number; a matrix that is singular or can become singular if some of its entries are changed ever so slightly.
The real vector, denoted by Im $\mathbf{x}$, formed by taking the coefficient of the imaginary part of each entry in a complex vector $\mathbf{x}$.
image(of a vector$\textbf{x}$ under a transformation$T$)
The vector $T(\textbf{x})$ assigned to $\textbf{x}$ by $T$.
The vector in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ formed from the imaginary parts of the entries of a vector $\textbf{x}$ in $\textbf{ℂ}^{n}$.
Refers to a system of equations that does not have any solutions.
A linear system with no solution.
A symmetric matrix ﻿$A$ such that $\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$﻿ assumes both positive and negative values.
A quadratic form $Q$ such that $Q(\textbf{x})$ assumes both positive and negative values.
A linear programming problem where the feasible set is empty.
infinite-dimensional (vector space)
A nonzero vector space $V$﻿ that has no finite basis.
A linear difference or differential equation with a specified initial value.

The scalar $\textbf{u}^{T}\textbf{v}$, usually written as $\textbf{u} \cdot \textbf{v}$, where $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are vectors in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ viewed as $n \times 1$ matrices. Also called the dot product of $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$. In general, a function on a vector space that assigns to each pair of vectors $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ a number $\langle\textbf{u},\textbf{v}\rangle$, subject to certain axioms.
A vector space on which an inner product is defined.
A matrix in the Leontief input–output model whose columns are the unit consumption vectors for the various sectors of an economy.
SeeLeontief input–output model.
interior point (of a set$S$in$\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$)
A point $\textbf{p}$ in $S$ such that for some $\delta\operatorname{\& gt;}0$, the open ball $\textbf{B}(\textbf{p},\delta)$ centered at $\textbf{p}$ is contained in $S$.

Demands for goods or services that will be consumed in the process of producing other goods and services for consumers. If $\textbf{x}$ is the production level and $C$ is the consumption matrix, then $C\textbf{x}$ lists the intermediate demands.
A polynomial whose graph passes through every point in a set of data points in $\text{ℝ}^{2}$.
invariant subspace(for $A$)
A subspace $H$ such that $A\textbf{x}$ is in $H$ whenever $\textbf{x}$ is in $H$.
inverse(of an $n \times n$ matrix $A$) An $n \times n$ matrix $A^{- 1}$ such that ﻿$AA^{- 1} = A^{- 1}A = I_{n}$.
An algorithm for estimating an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of a square matrix, when a good initial estimate of $\lambda$ is available.

A linear transformation $T:\textbf{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ such that there exists a function $S:\textbf{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ satisfying both $T(S(\textbf{x})) = \textbf{x}$ and $S(T(\textbf{x})) = \textbf{x}$ for all $\textbf{x}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$.
A square matrix that possesses an inverse.
Two vector spaces $V$ and $W$ for which there is a one-to-one linear transformation $T$ that maps $V$ onto $W$.
A one-to-one linear mapping from one vector space onto another.
glossary.heading: K
glossary.paragraph: kernel(of a linear transformation$T:V\rightarrow W)$
The set of $\textbf{x}$﻿ in ﻿$V$ such that ﻿$T\left( \textbf{x} \right) = \textbf{0}$.

(1) (voltage law) The algebraic sum of the $RI$ voltage drops in one direction around a loop equals the algebraic sum of the voltage sources in the same direction around the loop. (2) (current law) The current in a branch is the algebraic sum of the loop currents flowing through that branch.
glossary.heading: L
glossary.paragraph: An electrical network assembled by connecting in series two or more electrical circuits.
The leftmost nonzero entry in a row of a matrix.

The distance $\parallel \textbf{b} - A\widehat{\textbf{x}} \parallel$ from $\textbf{b}$ to $A\widehat{\textbf{x}}$, when $\widehat{\textbf{x}}$ is a least-squares solution of $A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$.
The line $y = {\widehat{\beta}}_{0} + {\widehat{\beta}}_{1}x$ that minimizes the least-squares error in the equation $\textbf{y} = X\mathbf{\beta}\mathbf{+}\mathbf{\in}$.
A vector $\widehat{\textbf{x}}$ such that $\parallel \textbf{b} - A\widehat{\textbf{x}} \parallel \leq \parallel \textbf{b} - A\textbf{x} \parallel$ for all $\textbf{x}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$.
left-multiplication(by $A$)
Multiplication of a vector or matrix on the left by $A$.
The columns of ﻿$U$ in the singular value decomposition $A = U\Sigma V^{T}$.﻿
length(or norm, of $\mathbf{v}$)
The scalar $\text{∥}\textbf{v}\text{∥} = \sqrt{\textbf{v} \cdot \textbf{v}} = \sqrt{\langle\textbf{v},\textbf{v}\rangle}$.

The equation $\textbf{x} = C\textbf{x} + \textbf{d}$, where $\textbf{x}$ is production, $\textbf{d}$ is final demand, and $C$ is the consumption (or input–output) matrix. The $j$th column of $C$ lists the inputs that sector $j$ consumes per unit of output.
A set $\left\lbrack {f:d} \right\rbrack\, = \left\{ {\textbf{x} \in \textbf{ℝ}^{n}:f\left( \textbf{x} \right) = d} \right\}$
Describes a transformation that preserves vector addition and scalar multiplication.
A sum of scalar multiples of vectors. The scalars are called the weights.
A homogeneous vector equation where the weights are all specified and at least one weight is nonzero.
linear equation(in the variables$x_{1}$, $\ldots$, $x_{n}$)﻿
An equation that can be written in the form $a_{1}x_{1} + a_{2}x_{2} + \cdots + a_{n}x_{n} = b$, where $b$ and the coefficients $a_{1}$, $\ldots$, $a_{n}$ are real or complex numbers.

paragraph.strong: line of regression of y on x

glossary.paragraph: The least squares line.
A linear difference equation used to transform discrete-time signals.
linearly dependent(vectors)

An indexed set $\left\{ \textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p} \right\}$ with the property that there exist weights $c_{1}$$...$ , $c_{p}$, not all zero, such that $c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + \cdots + c_{p}\textbf{v}_{p} = \textbf{0}$. That is, the vector equation $c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + c_{2}\textbf{v}_{2} + \cdots + c_{p}\textbf{v}_{p} = \textbf{0}$ has a nontrivial solution.
A linear transformation $f$ from $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ into $\text{ℝ}$.
See linear difference equation.
A linear transformation that is also time invariant.
A linear time invariant transformation used to remove undesired noise from a signal.
linearly independent(vectors)

An indexed set $\left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$﻿ with the property that the vector equation ﻿$c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + c_{2}\textbf{v}_{2} + \cdots + c_{p}\textbf{v}_{p} = \textbf{0}$ has only the trivial solution, $c_{1} = \cdots = c_{p} = 0$﻿.
linear model(in statistics)

Any equation of the form $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{x}\mathbf{\beta} + \mathbf{\varepsilon}$, where $X$ and $\textbf{y}$ are known and $\mathbf{\beta}$ is to be chosen to minimize the length of the residual vector, $\mathbf{\varepsilon}$.
A collection of one or more linear equations involving the same variables, say, $x_{1}$, $\ldots$, $x_{n}$.
linear transformation$\mathbf{T}$ (from a vector space $V$ into a vector space $W$)

A rule $T$ that assigns to each vector $\mathbf{x}$ in $V$ a unique vector $T\left( \textbf{x} \right)$ in $W$, such that (i) $T(\textbf{u} + \textbf{v}) = T(\textbf{u}) + T(\textbf{v})$ for all $\textbf{u},\textbf{v}$ in $V$ , and (ii) $T\,(c\textbf{u}) = cT\,(\textbf{u})$ for all $\textbf{u}$ in $V$ and all scalars $c$. Notation: $T:V\rightarrow W$; also, $\textbf{x}\mapsto A\textbf{x}$ when $T:\textbf{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\textbf{ℝ}^{m}$ and $A$ is the standard matrix for $T$ .
The amount of electric current flowing through a loop that makes the algebraic sum of the $RI$ voltage drops around the loop equal to the algebraic sum of the voltage sources in the loop.
A matrix with zeros above the main diagonal.
The representation of a matrix $A$ in the form $A = LU$ where $L$ is a square lower triangular matrix with ones on the diagonal and $U$ is an echelon form of $A$.
glossary.heading: M
glossary.paragraph: magnitude(of a vector)
The scalar $\parallel \textbf{v} \parallel = \sqrt{\textbf{v} \cdot \textbf{v}} = \sqrt{\langle\textbf{v},\textbf{v}\rangle}$.
main diagonal(of a matrix)
The entries with equal row and column indices.
Seetransformation.

A sequence of probability vectors $\textbf{x}_{0}$, $\textbf{x}_{1}$, $\textbf{x}_{2},\ldots,$ together with a stochastic matrix $P$ such that $\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = P\textbf{x}_{k}$ for $k = 0$, $1$, $2$, $\ldots$.
A rectangular array of numbers.
An equation that involves at least one matrix; for instance, $A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$.
The matrix representation of $T$ relative to a basis $B$.
A $p \times N$﻿ matrix whose columns are observation vectors, each column listing $p$﻿ measurements made on an individual or object in a specified population or set.
A mapping $\textbf{x}\mapsto A\textbf{x}$, where $A$ is an $m \times n$ matrix and $\textbf{x}$ represents any vector in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$.
A linearly independent set $S$ in $V$ such that if a vector in $V$ but not in $S$ is added to $S$, then the new set is linearly dependent.
mean-deviation form(of a matrix of observations) A matrix whose row vectors are in mean-deviation form. For each row, the entries sum to zero.
mean-deviation form(of a vector)
A vector whose entries sum to zero.
The error of an approximation in an inner product space, where the inner product is defined by a definite integral.
A matrix that gives the percentage movement between different locations, from one period to the next.
A set of points whose affine hull is the polytope $P$, but if any point is removed from the set, it no longer generates $P$.
A set $S$ that spans $H$ and has the property that if one of the elements of $S$ is removed from $S$, then the new set does not span $H$.
A signal created from another signal by taking the average of several consecutive terms.
A matrix with $m$ rows and $n$ columns.
The matrix $VD^{- 1}U^{T}$, when $UDV^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A$. ﻿
A linear model involving several independent variables and one dependent variable.
glossary.heading: N
glossary.paragraph: An approximation to a function using a trigonometric polynomial.
An ill-conditioned matrix.
A symmetric matrix ﻿$A$ ﻿ such that ﻿$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x~}\text{<~0}$ ﻿ for all ﻿﻿$\textbf{x~}\text{≠~0}$ .
A quadratic form ﻿$Q$ such that ﻿$Q\left( \textbf{x} \right) < 0$ for all ﻿$\textbf{x~}\text{≠~0}$ .
A symmetric matrix $A$ such that $\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x} \leq 0$ for all $\textbf{x}$.
A quadratic form $Q$ such that ﻿$Q\left( \textbf{x} \right) \leq 0$ for all ﻿$\textbf{x}$ .
Refers to the case where a system of equations, written in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$, has at least one nonzero entry in $\mathbf{b}$.
A matrix that is invertible.
A nonzero solution of a system of homogeneous equations.
nonzero(matrix or vector)
A matrix or vector that contains at least one nonzero entry.
norm(or length, of $\mathbf{v}$)
The scalar $\parallel \textbf{v} \parallel = \sqrt{\textbf{v} \cdot \textbf{v}} = \sqrt{\langle\textbf{v},\textbf{v}\rangle}$.
The process of creating a unit vector $\textbf{u}$ that is a positive multiple of $\mathbf{v}$.
A vector $\textbf{n}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ such that $\textbf{n} \cdot \textbf{x} = 0$ for all $\textbf{x}$ in a given subspace $W$.

For an $m \times n$ matrix $A$, the set $\text{Nul}\,A$ of all solutions to the homogeneous equation $A\textbf{x} = \textbf{0}$. $\text{Nul}\,A = \{\textbf{x}:\textbf{x}$ is in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ and $\left. A\textbf{x} = \textbf{0} \right\}$.
The dimension of the null space.
glossary.heading: O
glossary.paragraph: The function to be optimized over a given set of constraints.
The vector ﻿$\textbf{y}$ in the linear model $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{x}\mathbf{\beta} + \mathbf{\in}$, where the entries in $\textbf{y}$ are the observed values of a dependent variable.
one-to-one(mapping)
A mapping $T:\text{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\text{ℝ}^{m}$ such that each $\textbf{b}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{m}$ is the image of at most one $\textbf{x}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$.
onto(mapping)
A mapping $T:\text{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\text{ℝ}^{m}$ such that each $\textbf{b}$ in $R^{m}$ is the image of at least one $\textbf{x}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$.
open ball$\textbf{B}(\textbf{p},\delta)$in$\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$
The set $\left\{ \textbf{x}:\, \parallel \textbf{x} - \textbf{p} \parallel < ~\delta \right\}$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$, where $\delta\operatorname{\& gt;}0$.
open set$S$in$\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$
A set that contains none of its boundary points. (Equivalently, $S$ is open if every point of $S$ is an interior point.)
A strategy that provides the value of the game to a player.
A solution for which the objective function is as large as possible.
The zero vector.
A basis that is also an orthogonal set.
orthogonal complement(of $W)$
The set $W^{\bot}$ of all vectors orthogonal to $W$.
The representation of a vector y as the sum of two vectors, one in a specified subspace $W$ and the other in $W^{\bot}$.
orthogonally diagonalizable(matrix)
A matrix $A$﻿ that admits a factorization, $A = PDP^{- 1}$﻿, with $P$﻿ an orthogonal matrix ﻿$\text{(}P^{- 1} = P^{T}\text{)}$ and $D$﻿ diagonal.
A square invertible matrix $U$ such that $U^{- 1} = U^{T}$.

paragraph.strong: orthogonal projection of y onto L

glossary.paragraph: The vector in the direction of $L$ when $\mathbf{y}$ is written as the sum of a vector in the direction of $L$ and a vector orthogonal to $L$.
The vector $\widehat{\textbf{y}}$ defined by $\widehat{\textbf{y}} = \frac{\textbf{y} \cdot \textbf{u}}{\textbf{u} \cdot \textbf{u}}\textbf{u}$.
The unique vector $\widehat{\textbf{y}}$ in $W$ such that $\textbf{y} - \widehat{\textbf{y}}$ is orthogonal to $W$. Notation: $\widehat{\textbf{y}} = \text{proj}_{W}\text{\,\,}\textbf{y}$.
A set $S$ of vectors such that $\textbf{u} \cdot \textbf{v} = 0$ for each distinct pair $\textbf{u},\textbf{v}$ in $S$.
Orthogonal to every vector in $W$.
A basis that is an orthogonal set of unit vectors.
An orthogonal set of unit vectors.

A matrix product $\textbf{u}\textbf{v}^{T}$ where $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are vectors in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ viewed as $n \times 1$ matrices. (The transpose symbol is on the “outside” of the symbols $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$.)
A system of equations with more equations than unknowns.
glossary.heading: P
glossary.paragraph: Two or more flats such that each flat is a translate of the other flats.
A geometric interpretation of the sum of two vectors $\textbf{u}$, $\mathbf{v}$ as the diagonal of the parallelogram determined by $\textbf{u}$, $\mathbf{v}$, and $\textbf{0}$.
The unknown vector $\mathbf{\beta}$ in the linear model $\mathbf{y = x}\mathbf{\beta}\mathbf{+}\mathbf{\in}$.
An equation of the form $\textbf{x} = \textbf{p} + t\textbf{v}$ ($t$ in $\textbf{ℝ}$).
An equation of the form $\textbf{x} = \textbf{p} + s\textbf{u} + t\textbf{v}$ ($s$, $t$ in $\textbf{ℝ}$), with $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ linearly independent.
Using parameters (that vary over all real numbers) and vectors to describe all the vectors in the solution set of a system of equations.
Expressing the solutions set of a system of equations using parameters (that vary over all real numbers) and vectors.
The practice of interchanging rows in a matrix so that the pivot can be chosen to be the eligible entry in the column with the largest absolute value.
partitioned matrix(orblock matrix)
A matrix whose entries are themselves matrices of appropriate sizes.
A matrix such that a permutation of its rows will form a lower triangular matrix.
The representation of a matrix $A$ in the form $A = LU$ where $L$ is a square matrix such that a permutation of its rows will form a unit lower triangular matrix, and $U$ is an echelon form of $A$.
A signal in which the entries are repeated after a fixed length of time.
A nonzero number that either is used in a pivot position to create zeros through row operations or is changed into a leading $1$, which in turn is used to create zeros.
A column that contains a pivot position.
A position in a matrix $A$ that corresponds to a leading entry in an echelon form of $A$.
A set whose parametric equation is $\textbf{x} = s\textbf{u} + t\textbf{v}$ ($s$, $t$ in $\textbf{ℝ}$), with $\textbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ linearly independent.
A factorization $A = PQ$, where $P$ is an $n \times n$ positive semidefinite matrix with the same rank as $A$, and $Q$ is an $n \times n$ orthogonal matrix.
A polytope in $\textbf{ℝ}^{2}$.
A polytope in $\textbf{ℝ}^{3}$.
The convex hull of a finite set of points in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ (a special type of compact convex set).
A linear combination $c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + \cdots + c_{m}\textbf{v}_{m}$, where all $c_{i} \geq 0$.
A symmetric matrix ﻿﻿$A$ such that $\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}~ > 0$ for all $\textbf{x} \neq 0$﻿﻿.
A quadratic form ﻿$Q$ such that ﻿$Q\left( \textbf{x} \right)~ > 0$ for all ﻿$\text{x} \neq 0$.
The set of all positive combinations of points in $S$, denoted by $\text{pos\,\,}S$.
A symmetric matrix ﻿﻿$A$ such that ﻿$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}\text{~≥~0}$ ﻿ for all ﻿$\textbf{x}$. ﻿
A quadratic form ﻿ $Q$ such that ﻿$Q\left( \textbf{x} \right) \geq 0$ for all ﻿ $\textbf{x}$.﻿
An algorithm for estimating a strictly dominant eigenvalue of a square matrix.
The columns of the matrix that changes a quadratic form into one with no cross terms.
The unit eigenvectors of the covariance matrix.
A vector in ﻿$\text{ℝ}^{n}$ whose entries are nonnegative and sum to one.
The vector created by taking the linear combination of the columns of $A$ using the corresponding entries in $\mathbf{x}$ as weights.
The vector in the Leontief input–output model that lists the amounts that are to be produced by the various sectors of an economy.
The set of extreme points of $S$.
A matrix ﻿$B$ such that $B^{2} = B$﻿.
A subset of $S$ that does not equal $S$ itself.
Any subspace of a vector space $V$ other than $V$ itself.
pseudoinverse (of﻿$A$)
The matrix ﻿ $VD^{- 1}U^{T}$, when ﻿ $UDV^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A$.
The strategy where one entry in the strategy is one, and all other entries are zero.
glossary.heading: Q
glossary.paragraph: A factorization of an $m \times n$ matrix $A$ with linearly independent columns, $A = QR$, where $Q$ is an $m \times n$ matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis for $\text{Col\,\,}A$, and $R$ is an $n \times n$ upper triangular invertible matrix with positive entries on its diagonal.

A curve whose description may be written in the form $\textbf{g}(t) = (1 - t)\textbf{f}_{0}(t) + t\textbf{f}_{1}(t)$ for $0 \leq t \leq 1$, where $\textbf{f}_{0}(t) = (1 - t)\textbf{p}_{0} + t\textbf{p}_{1}$ and $\textbf{f}_{1}(t) = (1 - t)\textbf{p}_{1} + t\textbf{p}_{2}$. The points $\textbf{p}_{0}$, $\textbf{p}_{1}$, $\textbf{p}_{2}$ are called the control points for the curve.

A function ﻿$Q$ defined for ﻿$\textbf{x}$ in ﻿$\text{ℝ}^{n}$ by ﻿$Q(\textbf{x}) = \mathbf{x}^{T}\mspace{-4mu} A\textbf{x}$ , where ﻿ $A$ is an ﻿$n \times n$ symmetric matrix (called the matrix of the quadratic form).
glossary.heading: R
glossary.paragraph: range(of a linear transformation $T$)
The set of all vectors of the form $T\left( \textbf{x} \right)$﻿ for some ﻿$\textbf{x}$ in the domain of ﻿$T$ .
rank(of a matrix $A$)
The dimension of the column space of $A$, denoted by rank$\,A$.
$R(\textbf{x}) = (\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x})/(\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x})$. An estimate of an eigenvalue of $A$ (usually a symmetric matrix).
The real vector, denoted by Re $\mathbf{x}$, formed by taking the real part of each entry in a complex vector $\mathbf{x}$.
reduced echelon form (or reduced row echelon form)
A reduced echelon matrix that is row equivalent to a given matrix.
A rectangular matrix in echelon form that has these additional properties: The leading entry in each nonzero row is $1$, and each leading $1$ is the only nonzero entry in its column.

A factorization ﻿$A = UDV^{T}$, for an ﻿$m \times n$ matrix ﻿$A$ of rank ﻿$r$ , where ﻿$U$ is ﻿$m \times r$ with orthonormal columns, ﻿$D$ is an ﻿ $r \times r$ diagonal matrix with the ﻿ $r$ nonzero singular values of ﻿ $A$ on its diagonal, and ﻿$V$ is ﻿$n \times r$ with orthonormal columns.
The coefficients $\beta_{0}$ and $\beta_{1}$ in the least-squares line $y = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1}x$.

One of the five possible regular polyhedrons in $\textbf{ℝ}^{3}$: the tetrahedron ($4$ equal triangular faces), the cube ($6$ square faces), the octahedron ($8$ equal triangular faces), the dodecahedron ($12$ equal pentagonal faces), and the icosahedron ($20$ equal triangular faces).
A stochastic matrix $P$ such that some matrix power $P^{k}$ contains only strictly positive entries.
relative changeorrelative error(in$\textbf{b}$)﻿
The quantity $\parallel \Delta\textbf{b}\mspace{-4mu} \parallel / \parallel \mspace{-4mu}\textbf{b} \parallel$ when $\textbf{b}$ is changed to $\textbf{b} + \Delta\textbf{b}$.
The origin of a dynamical system when all trajectories except the constant zero sequence or function tend away from $\textbf{0}$.

The quantity $\mathbf{\varepsilon}$ that appears in the general linear model: $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{X}\mathbf{\beta} + \mathbf{\varepsilon}$; that is, $\mathbf{\varepsilon} = \mathbf{y}\, - \,\mathbf{X}\mspace{-4mu}\mathbf{\beta}$, the difference between the observed values and the predicted values (of $y$).
The vector in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ formed from the real parts of the entries of a vector $\textbf{x}$ in $\textbf{ℂ}^{n}$.
right singular vectors (of$A$)
The columns of $V$ in the singular value decomposition $A = U\text{Σ}V^{T}$.

Error in floating point arithmetic caused when the result of a calculation is rounded (or truncated) to the number of floating point digits stored. Also, the error that results when the decimal representation of a number such as $1/3$ is approximated by a floating point number with a finite number of digits.
The rule for computing a product $AB$ in which the $(i,j)\text{-entry}$ of $AB$ is the sum of the products of corresponding entries from row $i$ of $A$ and column $j$ of $B$.
row equivalent (matrices)
Two matrices for which there exists a (finite) sequence of row operations that transforms one matrix into the other.
Transformed by elementary row operations into an echelon form.
A systematic method using elementary row operations that reduces a matrix to echelon form or reduced echelon form.
An elementary row operation that replaces one row of a matrix by the sum of the row and a multiple of another row.
row space(of a matrix $A$)
The set Row $A$ of all linear combinations of the vectors formed from the rows of $A$; also denoted by $\text{Col~}A^{T}$.
The sum of the entries in a row of a matrix.
A matrix with only one row, or a single row of a matrix that has several rows.

The rule for computing a product $A\textbf{x}$ in which the $i\text{th}$ entry of $A\textbf{x}$ is the sum of the products of corresponding entries from row $i$ of $A$ and from the vector $\textbf{x}$.
glossary.heading: S
glossary.paragraph: The origin when some trajectories are attracted to $\textbf{0}$ and other trajectories are repelled from $\textbf{0}$.
sample mean﻿
The average $\mathbf{M}$ of a set of vectors, $\textbf{X}_{1}$﻿, $\ldots$ , $\textbf{X}_{N}$, given by $\mathbf{M} = (1/N)\left( \textbf{X}_{1} + \cdots + \textbf{X}_{N} \right)$.
A (real) number used to multiply either a vector or a matrix.
The vector or matrix obtained by multiplying every entry in a given vector or matrix by the same constant.
scale (a vector)
Multiply a vector (or a row or column of a matrix) by a nonzero scalar.

A certain matrix formed from the blocks of a $2 \times 2$ partitioned matrix $A = \lbrack A_{ij}\rbrack$. If $A_{11}$ is invertible, its Schur complement is given by $A_{22} - A_{21}A_{11}^{- 1}A_{12}$. If $A_{22}$ is invertible, its Schur complement is given by $A_{11} - A_{12}A_{22}^{- 1}A_{21}$.
Schur factorization (of ﻿﻿$A$﻿, for real scalars)
A factorization $A = URU^{T}$ of an $n \times n$ matrix $A$ having $n$ real eigenvalues, where $U$ is an $n \times n$ orthogonal matrix and $R$ is an upper triangular matrix.
set spanned by ﻿﻿$\left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$
The set Span $\left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$.
A transformation that maps a square onto a parallelogram with the same height and base.
signal(or discrete-time signal)
A doubly infinite sequence of numbers, $\left. \{ y_{k} \right\}$; ﻿a function defined on the integers; belongs to the vector space $\mathbb{S}$.﻿
The origin when all trajectories tend toward 0.
similar (matrices)
Matrices $A$ and $B$ such that $P^{- 1}AP = B$, or equivalently, $A = PBP^{- 1}$, for some invertible matrix $P.$
A transformation that changes $A$ into $P^{- 1}AP$.
The convex hull of an affinely independent finite set of vectors in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$.
The set of signals where the only nonzero entries in a signal have subscripts from $0$ to $n$.
A matrix that is not invertible.
singular value decomposition(of an $m \times n$﻿﻿﻿ matrix $A$﻿﻿﻿)

$A = U\text{Σ}V^{T}$, where $U$ is an $m \times m$ orthogonal matrix, $V$ is an $n \times n$ orthogonal matrix, and $\Sigma$ is an $m \times n$ matrix with nonnegative entries on the main diagonal (arranged in decreasing order of magnitude) and zeros elsewhere. If rank $A = r$, then $\Sigma$ has exactly $r$ positive entries (the nonzero singular values of $A$) on the diagonal.
singular values(of $A$)
The (positive) square roots of the eigenvalues of $A^{T}A$﻿, arranged in decreasing order of magnitude.
size(of a matrix)
Two numbers, written in the form $m \times n$, that specify the number of rows $(m)$ and columns $(n)$ in the matrix.
A variable added to an inequality to change it into an equality.
solution(of a linear system involving variables ﻿﻿$x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}$)﻿
A list $(s_{1},s_{2},\ldots,s_{n})$ of numbers that makes each equation in the system a true statement when the values $s_{1},\ldots,s_{n}$ are substituted for $x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}$, respectively.
The set of all possible solutions of a linear system. The solution set is empty when the linear system is inconsistent.
The set of all linear combinations of $\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}$. Also, the subspace spanned (or generated) by $\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}$.
﻿The span of the vectors in the given set is all of $\text{ℝ}^{m}$.
spanning set (for a subspace $H$)﻿
Any set $\left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$ in $H$ such that $H = \text{Span~}\left\{ {\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}} \right\}$.
spectral decomposition(of $A$)
A representation
where $\left\{ \textbf{u}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{u}_{n} \right\}$﻿ is an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of $A$﻿, and $\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{n}$﻿ are the corresponding eigenvalues of ﻿$A$.
spiral point(of a dynamical system in $\textbf{ℝ}^{2}$)
The origin when the trajectories spiral about $0$.

A difference equation $\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$ where $\textbf{x}_{k}$ lists the number of females in a population at time $k$, with the females classified by various stages of development (such as juvenile, subadult, and adult).

The basis $\varepsilon = \{\textbf{e}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{e}_{n}\}$ for $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$ consisting of the columns of the $n \times n$ identity matrix, or the basis $\{ 1,t,\ldots,t^{n}\}$ for ﻿﻿$\textbf{ℙ}_{n}$.

paragraph.strong: standard matrix for the linear transformation

glossary.paragraph: Matrix representation of a linear transformation created using the standard basis vectors.
standard matrix (for a linear transformation $T$)﻿
The matrix $A$ such that $T(\textbf{x}) = A\textbf{x}$ for all $\textbf{x}$ in the domain of $T$.
The position of the graph of an equation $\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x} = c$, when $A$ is a diagonal matrix.
A probability vector. In general, a vector that describes the “state” of a physical system, often in connection with a difference equation $\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$.
steady-state vector(for a stochastic matrix $\mathbf{P}$﻿﻿﻿)
A probability vector $\textbf{q}$ such that $P\textbf{q} = \textbf{q}$.

The inverse of a flexibility matrix. The $j\text{th}$ column of a stiffness matrix gives the loads that must be applied at specified points on an elastic beam in order to produce a unit deflection at the $j\text{th}$ point on the beam.
A square matrix whose columns are probability vectors.
The set of vectors that describes all possible strategies for a given player.
An eigenvalue $\lambda_{1}$ of a matrix $A$ with the property that $|\lambda_{1}|\operatorname{\& gt;}|\lambda_{k}|$ for all other eigenvalues $\lambda_{k}$ of $A$.
submatrix(of$A$)
Any matrix obtained by deleting some rows and/or columns of $A$﻿; also, $A$ itself.

A subset $H$ of some vector space $V$ such that $H$ has these properties: (1) the zero vector of $V$ is in $H$; (2) $H$ is closed under vector addition; and (3) $H$ is closed under multiplication by scalars.
The subset created by taking all possible linear combinations of a given set of vectors.
The vector or matrix obtained by adding corresponding entries in two given vectors or matrices of the same size.
supporting hyperplane(to a compact convex set $S$ in $\textbf{ℝ}^{n}$)
A hyperplane $H = \lbrack f:d\rbrack$﻿ such that $H \cap S \neq \varnothing$ and either $f(x) \leq d$ for all $x$ in $S$ or $f(x) \geq d$ for all $x$ in $S$.
A matrix $A$ such that $A^{T}$ = $A$.
system of linear equations (or a linear system)
A collection of one or more linear equations involving the same set of variables, say, $x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}$.
glossary.heading: T
glossary.paragraph: A vector describing the direction of a curve at a given point.

paragraph.strong: the best approximation to y by elements of W

glossary.paragraph: A vector in $W$ that is the same distance from or closer to $\mathbf{y}$ than all the other vectors in $W$.
The trace of the covariance matrix ﻿$S$ of a matrix of observations.
trace(of a square matrix ﻿$A$)
The sum of the diagonal entries in ﻿$A$, denoted by $\text{tr\,\,}A$.

The graph of a solution $\left\{ {\textbf{x}_{0},\textbf{x}_{1},\textbf{x}_{2},\ldots} \right\}$ of a dynamical system $\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$, often connected by a thin curve to make the trajectory easier to see. Also, the graph of $\textbf{x}(t)$ for $t \geq 0$, when $\textbf{x}(t)$ is a solution of a differential equation $\textbf{x}^{\prime}(t) = A\textbf{x}(t)$.
A matrix $A$ associated with an electrical circuit having input and output terminals, such that the output vector is $A$ times the input vector.
transformation(or function, ormapping)Tfrom$\text{ℝ}^{n}$to$\text{ℝ}^{m}$

A rule that assigns to each vector $\textbf{x}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ a unique vector $T(\textbf{x})$ in $\text{ℝ}^{m}$. Notation: $T\mspace{-4mu}:\text{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\text{ℝ}^{m}$. Also, $T\mspace{-4mu}:V\rightarrow W$ denotes a rule that assigns to each $\textbf{x}$ in $V$ a unique vector $T(\textbf{x})$ in $W$.
transpose(of ﻿$A$)
An $n \times m$ matrix $A^{T}$ whose columns are the corresponding rows of the $m \times n$ matrix $A$.
The use of orthogonal polynomials to fit data, with the inner product given by evaluation at a finite set of points.
The coefficients of each polynomial used to create a trend function.
The function that approximates the behavior of measured data over time.
$\parallel \textbf{u} + \textbf{v} \parallel \, \leq \, \parallel \textbf{u} \parallel + \parallel \textbf{v~} \parallel$ for all $\textbf{u}$, $\mathbf{v}$.
A pattern of zeros in a matrix forming a triangle in the lower left or upper right corner.
A linear combination of the constant function $1$ and sine and cosine functions such as $\cos nt$ and $\sin nt$.
The solution $\textbf{x} = \textbf{0}$ of a homogeneous equation $A\textbf{x} = \textbf{0}$.
glossary.heading: U
glossary.paragraph: Any two variables $x_{i}$﻿ and ﻿$x_{j}$ (with $i \neq j$﻿) that range over the $\textit{i\,}\text{th}$﻿ and $j{th}$﻿ coordinates of the observation vectors in an observation matrix, such that the covariance $s_{ij}$﻿ is zero.
A linear programming problem where the objective function is unbounded on the feasible set.
A system of equations with fewer equations than unknowns.
Asks, “If a solution of a system exists, is it unique—that is, is it the only one?”
A column vector in the Leontief input–output model that lists the inputs a sector needs for each unit of its output; a column of the consumption matrix.
A square lower triangular matrix with ones on the main diagonal.
A vector $\mathbf{v}$ such that $\text{∥}\textbf{v}\text{∥} = 1$.
A matrix $U$ (not necessarily square) with zeros below the diagonal entries ﻿$u_{11},u_{22},\ldots$.
glossary.heading: V
glossary.paragraph: The result of the game when both players play the best strategy.

paragraph.strong: value of the game to column player C

glossary.paragraph: The worst that player $C$ can do if they always play the best strategy.

paragraph.strong: value of the game to row player R

glossary.paragraph: The worst that player $R$ can do if they always play the best strategy.
variance(of a variable $x_{j}$﻿)
The diagonal entry ﻿$s_{\textit{jj}}$ in the covariance matrix ﻿$S$ for a matrix of observations, where ﻿ $x_{j}$ varies over the ﻿$j\text{th}$ coordinates of the observation vectors.
